standard_prerequisites.name: First backward return time to a subinterval
standard_prerequisites.statement: b_J(c) is the first positive time the backward orbit of the point c enters the subinterval J.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the exponent governing the alternative in the conclusion.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induced transformation and its centres
standard_prerequisites.statement: The induced transformation on J exchanges its continuity intervals, and the centres of those intervals are the points fixed by the conjugate of the induced transformation.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the possible values of the projected point in the first alternative.

standard_prerequisites.name: Connections
standard_prerequisites.statement: A connection is a finite orbit fragment joining two discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the second alternative forces for the centre.

core_obligations: In the first alternative, where the relevant orbit fragment avoids the discontinuities, use the backward-iterate formula together with the local reflection lemma to identify the first visit time of the centre to the subinterval under the induced transformation (source lines 778-785).
Show that the projected point is a fixed point of the conjugate of the induced transformation, applying the conjugacy identity for iterates and the local reflection lemma (source lines 787-795).
Conclude that the projected point is a centre of a continuity interval of the induced transformation, since such points are exactly the fixed points of that conjugate (source line 795).

In the second alternative, take the first exponent at which the orbit meets a discontinuity and apply the criterion that a centre meeting the discontinuities lies in a non-trivial connection (source lines 797-800).

proof_roadmap.step: First alternative: identify the first visit time to the subinterval.
Show the projected point is fixed by the conjugate of the induced transformation, hence a centre.
Second alternative: locate the first meeting with the discontinuities and conclude a connection.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled claim at source lines 761-775: for a centre other than the distinguished one, with first backward return time to the symmetric subinterval equal to l, either the orbit fragment up to the shifted exponent avoids the discontinuities and the projected point is a centre of the induced transformation satisfying an explicit identity, or that fragment meets the discontinuities and the projected point is an endpoint of the induced transformation while the centre lies in a non-trivial connection. The proof (source lines 777-800) runs the two alternatives with genuinely different arguments: in the first, the shift by the indicator has to be carried through the backward-iterate formula and the local reflection lemma before the projected point can be recognised as a fixed point of the conjugate of the induced transformation; in the second, the first meeting with the discontinuities has to be located before the connection criterion applies. The statement records the two alternatives and neither mechanism.
